title: Canonical Format Kind
description: Discriminator naming one of the 15 AdCP 3.2 canonical creative formats, plus `custom` for adopter-defined shapes. AdCP 3.2 adds `audio_vast` for VAST-tag-delivered audio (the standards-conformant profile starts at VAST 4.1, with older versions available only as seller-declared legacy interoperability) and promotes the legacy `multi_state_display` and `multi_placement_takeover` custom shapes to `seller_rendered_stateful_display` and `coordinated_placements`. When `format_kind` is `custom`, the declaration also carries `format_shape` and `format_schema`. The enum mirrors the branches in `product-format-declaration.json` and is closed for producer validation: sellers do not mint ad-hoc values. SDKs may retain unknown future values in tolerant in-memory parsers, but that does not change versioned JSON Schema validation. In a product format declaration, `format_kind` is the discriminator: each kind has its own branch in `product-format-declaration.json`, and an older release has no branch for a newer kind. A seller serving 3.1 or earlier MUST project a declaration with a 3.2-only kind to a compatible legacy declaration or omit it; a strict older schema correctly rejects an unprojected declaration. Everywhere else, a newer kind is a new enum value: it is exempt from projection ([Serving an older pin](/docs/reference/versioning#serving-an-older-pin)), and clients tolerate it under the [Enums](/docs/reference/versioning#3-x-stability-guarantees) rule. See adcp#3666 and the promotion migration contract in canonical-formats.mdx.
